howToPlay: You are the Flight Director. Hire a crew, build a capsule and choose a rocket. You have $800M and 46 days, and both run out fast.
Each week you assign staff and handle surprises. Every choice costs money, time or risk. There is rarely a perfect answer, only trade-offs.
Before launch, your crew votes Go or No-Go. Listen to them. Your choices decide whether the mission reaches orbit.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Welcome, Flight Director! You made it. Mind the paint, they're still finishing the hangar.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: I'm Rosa Vega. I spent most of my career running launches from Mission Control.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Officially I'm retired. Unofficially, I couldn't stay away from a good rocket.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: This agency is tiny, and it needs a leader who isn't afraid of a hard decision. That's you.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: You have $800 million and 46 days. Miss the launch window and it's gone, and so is the mission.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Before we start, every agency needs a name. What shall we put on the door?

scenes.agencyNamePrompt: What should we call our agency?

afterName.speaker: rosa
afterName.text: {agencyName}. I like it. It sounds like a place where good rockets get built.

missionCard.title: Mission 1
facts: Crew of three to low Earth orbit
Win: crew safe, in orbit, score 60 or more

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Here's your mission card. Get a crew of three to low Earth orbit, safely, with a score of 60 or better.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Think of a launch window like a train that leaves once. If you're late, it doesn't wait for you.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Winning means the crew is alive, the capsule is in orbit, and the books are in good shape. All three.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: See the bar along the top? That's your dashboard. Learn to read it. It's your best friend.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Budget is your money in millions. Run out and the mission is over, so spend like it's real.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Days shows how long until the launch window closes. Every delay eats into it.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Mass margin is how much extra weight your rocket can lift. Below zero, you're too heavy to fly.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Power compares what your systems use to what your capsule makes. Use more than you make and things shut down.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Comms is your radio. A weak one can't send science data home.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Morale is how the team feels. Tired, unhappy people do slower, sloppier work.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: There's one number you can't see, called reliability. It's how likely things are to work when it counts.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Good parts and careful testing raise it. Shortcuts and surprises lower it. Treat it kindly.

stops.name: Hire
stops.text: Hire a crew of three astronauts and any staff you can afford.

stops.name: Build
stops.text: Choose your capsule parts, rocket, launch site and orbit.

stops.name: Trail
stops.text: Spend five weeks assigning staff and facing surprises.

stops.name: Launch Week
stops.text: Study the forecast, pick your day, and hear your crew vote.

stops.name: Launch
stops.text: Press the button and find out what your choices were worth.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Every choice here costs you something. Money, time or risk. There's no free lunch in space.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: That's not a trap. That's the job.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Astronauts have three skills from one to five. Piloting flies, engineering fixes, and nerves keep a cool head.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Everyone has a flaw too. A great pilot who skips checklists can sink you faster than a rookie can.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Staff do the work behind the scenes. Without an engineer, an inspector or a meteorologist, you'll be guessing.

steady.speaker: rosa
steady.text: This crew keeps calm when it counts. That will matter on launch morning.

lightEngineering.speaker: rosa
lightEngineering.text: Your crew is light on engineering. Your staff will have to carry the repairs..

balanced.speaker: rosa
balanced.text: A balanced crew. Good. Nobody's too strong or too weak anywhere.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.text: Measure twice, launch once.

pilot.speaker: rosa
pilot.text: Piloting is flying skill. A strong pilot handles a rough launch better.

pilot.speaker: rosa
pilot.text: It can't fix a broken capsule, though. That's engineering's job.

eng.speaker: rosa
eng.text: Engineering is fixing things fast. If a system fails in orbit, this is who saves you.

eng.speaker: rosa
eng.text: Think of it as the crew's own toolbox.

nerves.speaker: rosa
nerves.text: Nerves is staying calm when alarms go off. High nerves means clear thinking in a crisis.

nerves.speaker: rosa
nerves.text: It also decides how quickly a crewmate votes No-Go.

engineer.speaker: rosa
engineer.text: Engineers build the capsule. The better they are, the fewer weeks it takes.

engineer.speaker: rosa
engineer.text: Build slowly and you run out of days. Build carelessly and you run out of luck.

inspector.speaker: rosa
inspector.text: Inspectors test and check everything. They catch hidden flaws before the rocket does.

inspector.speaker: rosa
inspector.text: Skip them and reliability quietly drops every week.

meteorologist.speaker: rosa
meteorologist.text: A meteorologist makes the forecast sharper. They can tell storms from showers days ahead.

meteorologist.speaker: rosa
meteorologist.text: Without one, you're guessing at the sky.

logistics.speaker: rosa
logistics.text: Logistics keeps parts arriving on time, with fewer stolen or late shipments.

logistics.speaker: rosa
logistics.text: Delays cost days, and days are the one thing you can't buy.

pr.speaker: rosa
pr.text: A PR lead turns your good work into donations. A good week of fundraising can pay for a part.

pr.speaker: rosa
pr.text: Budget is the thing everybody runs short on.
